{{recipesummary

}}

{{recipe}}

'''Radish tart''' is a tasty and colorful [[Cookbook:Pie|pie]], best served hot from the oven. Fresh red radishes and yellow cheese give this pretty pie an interesting look and taste.

==Ingredients==
*1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:All-purpose flour|all-purpose flour]]
*½ cup cold [[Cookbook:butter|butter]]
*1 cup (4 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) shredded Edam, Gouda, or Gruyere [[Cookbook:cheese|cheese]], divided ([[Cookbook:Cheddar Cheese|Cheddar]] is also acceptable)
*1 cup heavy [[Cookbook:cream|cream]], divided
*4 [[Cookbook:egg|egg]] yolks
*¼ tsp [[Cookbook:salt|salt]]
*½–1 small bunch of red [[Cookbook:radish|radishes]]

==Procedure==
#Preheat [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 425°F (220°C).
#[[Cookbook:Sifting|Sift]] and measure flour into a bowl. Cut in the butter until the particles are coarse. Stir in half of the cheese. Pour in ¼ cup of the cream; [[Cookbook:Mixing#Tossing|toss]] the mixture with a fork until all parts are moistened.
#Turn the dough into a 9-[[Cookbook:Inch|inch]] round [[Cookbook:Pie and Tart Pans|pie pan]]. With floured fingers, press the mixture into the bottom and sides of the pan, then prick the shell with a floured fork.
#[[Cookbook:Baking|Bake]] the pie shell for 10–12 minutes. The sides will slip down a little during baking. Cool on a [[Cookbook:Cooling Rack|wire rack]].
#Lower the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C).
#Sprinkle the remaining cheese evenly over the bottom of the cooled pie shell. [[Cookbook:Beating|Beat]] together the egg yolks, the ¾ cup cream, and the salt. Pour the egg mixture over the cheese. Place the radish slices evenly over the top of the pie.
#Bake for 20–25 minutes, or until set.
#Remove the pie from the oven, cut it into wedges, and serve it hot. 

==Notes, tips, and variations==
*If you really like the taste of radishes, use ½ cup or more. For a milder pie, use ¼ cup.
*The cheese crust has a pleasant crisp texture when eaten fresh out of the oven. Leftovers can be refrigerated and reheated later, but the texture will not be as good.
*A really sharp knife will aid in cutting the wedges without displacing the radishes.
